sections.html:
Frederick is Virginia's most northern county, and it curls around the city of Winchester. Winchester holds the county seat in name, though as an independent city it keeps its own offices. A Winchester mailing address could belong to either jurisdiction. Settle that question before dialing anyone, since the wrong office will only send you back.

The 2020 census found 91,419 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 99,955. Of 35,827 housing units, 78.8% of the occupied ones are owner-occupied. Two towns, Stephens City and Middletown, have their own governments. Many more homes lie in unincorporated spots like Kernstown, Clear Brook, Gainesboro, Round Hill, Jordan Springs, Lake Frederick and Mountain Falls, and their owners answer to the county only.

Real estate is taxed at $0.53 per $100 of assessed value, and mobile homes carry the identical figure. The county site offers a calculator where you can enter your own assessment and see a rough annual bill before you list.

Tax typeRate
Real estate$0.53 per $100 of assessed value
Personal property$4.35 per $100
County meals tax6.0%
Lodging tax6.0%

Each year's bill is split, with the first half due June 5 and the second due December 5. A closed office on the due date pushes the deadline to the next business day. The Treasurer runs a pre-pay option for people who prefer to get ahead. The Treasurer can quote the penalty in force right now, which you want before planning a payoff.

The Commissioner of the Revenue posts a calendar of the remaining dates a homeowner may meet during the year.

  • January 1 through April 1: elderly and permanently disabled relief applications, due April 1.
  • June 5: first half of real estate and personal property tax.
  • November 1: land use applications, with a late fee accepted through December 1.
  • December 5: second half.

Relief for former service members who are totally and permanently disabled with a 100 percent service-connected rating, and for surviving spouses of those killed in action, has no seasonal cutoff.

Your first stop is the assessor, reachable at 540-665-5680. You have grounds to appeal when the Commissioner of the Revenue made a mistake, or when someone else made a factual error during a general reassessment. A plain belief that the value runs high is worth raising there too, since staff can lay out how the figure was built.

Three routes are open.

  1. A hearing before the assessor at the County Administration Building, 107 North Kent Street, Winchester. Book it on 540-722-8319 between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m. on weekdays. Dates for hearings run in The Winchester Star and appear on the website.
  2. A written appeal, sent by email, by letter or on the Appeal of Assessment form, to Commissioner of the Revenue, Real Property Tax Appeal, PO Box 552, Winchester, VA 22604.
  3. Escalation to the Board of Equalization, then to the Frederick County Circuit Court.

Find out from the Commissioner's staff when the next reassessment cycle opens and which deadline governs the Board of Equalization. Virginia Code 58.1-3984 covers court timing, and a judge begins by presuming the assessor got a real property value right. Photos of defects and recent sales nearby carry the most weight.

Assessments for farm, horticultural and forest land use come out of the Real Estate Division inside the Commissioner's office. The division also processes relief for elderly and disabled owners, disabled former service members, and surviving spouses of certain persons killed in the line of duty, and it links a Tax Sale Information Center from its page.

If the parcel is enrolled in land use, find out from the division what happens to the deferral at sale, ideally before anyone picks a closing day. Rollback rules and who pays them can change the amount you walk away with. The program rules are linked from the division's page.

Owners of rural property should glance at the county home page for emergency notices, because a posted wildfire or weather update may change how you schedule showings.

sections.h2: If you owe tax at sale time
sections.html:
In Virginia, tax owed on a house jumps the line ahead of every other lien. Virginia Code 58.1-3340 keeps the lien alive until payment really happens. Money from a sale is aimed first at taxes and levies on that parcel, and the penalties and interest that pile up are treated as tax too. Which months of the current year belong to you is a matter for the sales contract.

Recording the deed brings a separate charge, the grantor's tax in Virginia Code 58.1-802. The rate is 50 cents per $500 of consideration. Sellers pay unless the buyer agrees to take it on.

Here is how a payoff usually plays out.

  1. Get a written balance from the Treasurer, itemized by tax, penalty and interest, along with the last day it stays accurate.
  2. Hand that sheet to whoever is running settlement.
  3. The Treasurer gets paid from your side of the settlement statement and the lien comes off the record.
  4. Tuck the paid receipt into your closing file.

sections.h2: How a sale moves through the county offices
sections.html:
Three offices touch a Frederick County sale. The assessor holds the value and the land use file. The Treasurer holds the payment record. The circuit court clerk records the deed. Late surprises usually trace to a balance that no one checked until the final week, so make the calls in this order.

  1. Call the assessor and confirm the parcel, the acreage and the assessed value on file. Fix any factual error now, while an appeal route is still open.
  2. Ask whether the property sits in land use or receives relief, and what a sale does to either.
  3. Request the Treasurer's payoff once you have a signed contract, and again close to settlement if the date slips past a due date.
  4. Decide in the contract who pays the grantor's tax, because the seller owes it by default.
  5. After closing, confirm the next bill goes to the new owner and that your account shows a zero balance.

A second half due December 5 or a first half due June 5 can fall in the middle of a sale. When that happens, the contract and the closing statement should say plainly which party pays that half, which avoids a bill landing on the wrong person after the keys change hands.

sections.h2: What to gather before you sell
sections.html:
Set out your latest tax bill, any assessment notice, a copy of the deed showing every owner, and the parcel number. If the land is in land use, or you get elderly or disabled relief, tell the closing agent early so that status is dealt with ahead of recording.

An inherited, empty or rented house, or one that needs work, can be hard to list. A cash sale skips the showings, the prep and the wait on a buyer's loan. Cash Home Buyers will look at a Frederick County house exactly as it stands, and the title company still settles any tax balance out of the proceeds. Whichever way you go, get the payoff on paper so you know what you will net.

faqs.q: What is the Frederick County real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: $0.53 for every $100 of assessed value, with mobile homes at the same figure.

faqs.q: When are Frederick County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: June 5 for the first half and December 5 for the second half. If the office is closed on a due date, the next business day applies.

faqs.q: Who do I call to dispute a Frederick County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the assessor at 540-665-5680. To schedule a hearing, call 540-722-8319 between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m. on weekdays.

faqs.q: Is Winchester part of Frederick County?
faqs.a: No. It hosts the county seat, yet Virginia law makes it an independent city that the county simply surrounds.

faqs.q: When is the Frederick County tax relief deadline for seniors?
faqs.a: Applications for elderly or permanently disabled relief are accepted from January 1 to April 1.
